hints.content:
###Graphing the equations

The equations are both in *slope intercept form*: $y=\goldD{m}x+\purpleC{b}$. We can use the $y$-intercept and slope to identify points on each line.

The line given by the first equation $y=\goldD{-2}x\purpleC{-5}
$ has a $y$-intercept of $(0,\purpleC{-5})$ and a slope of $\goldD{-2}$, so another point on that line is $(0+1,\purpleC{-5}\goldD{-2})=(1,-7).$ Now we have two points to graph this line.

In a similar manner, we can find that the line given by $y=\goldD{2}x\purpleC{-2}$ passes through $(0,\purpleC{-2})$ and $(0+1,\purpleC{-2}+\goldD{2})=(1,0)$.

We can graph the lines using these points:

[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A coordinate plane. The x- and y-axes both scale by one. The equation y equals negative two x minus five is graphed with the points zero, negative five and one, negative seven plotted on the line. The equation y equals two x minus two is graphed with the points zero, negative two and one, zero plotted on the line.

hints.content:
###Solving the system

When we graph the two lines, we can see that they intersect between $x=-1$ and $x=0$ and between $y=-4$ and $y=-3$:

[[☃ image 1]]

There is only one option that fits this description: $x= -\dfrac34, y=-3\dfrac12$.

options.alt: A coordinate plane. The x- and y-axes both scale by one. The equation y equals negative two x minus five is graphed with the points zero, negative five and one, negative seven plotted on the line. The equation y equals two x minus two is graphed with the points zero, negative two and one, zero plotted on the line. The intersection of these two lines is plotted at an x-value between negative one and zero and a y-value between negative four and negative three.
